reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / WHO nutrition guidance
clinicalPearls: Remembered by the triad of dermatitis, diarrhoea, and dementia, with death in untreated advanced disease
The rash is a symmetrical, photosensitive, pigmented dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, classically a collar-like band over the neck (Casal's necklace)
It occurs where maize or sorghum is the dietary staple because their niacin is poorly bioavailable and they are low in tryptophan
Chronic alcohol use, malabsorption, carcinoid syndrome, and isoniazid therapy are recognised precipitants
Neuropsychiatric features range from irritability and depression to confusion and frank dementia
A glossitis, stomatitis, and diarrhoea reflect involvement of the whole gastrointestinal mucosa
Clinical improvement after niacin repletion is rapid and helps confirm the diagnosis
reference.pathophysiology: Niacin, obtained from the diet or synthesised from tryptophan, is the precursor of the coenzymes NAD and NADP that are central to cellular energy metabolism and redox reactions. Deficiency impairs energy-dependent repair and turnover in tissues with high metabolic demand, explaining the prominence of skin, gut mucosa, and nervous system involvement. Diets based on untreated maize provide niacin in a bound, poorly absorbable form and little tryptophan; conditions that divert tryptophan, such as carcinoid tumours, or that impair absorption or metabolism, such as alcoholism and certain drugs, produce secondary deficiency.
additionalDifferentials: Other B-vitamin deficiencies with overlapping mucocutaneous signs
Dementia and confusional states from other causes
Carcinoid syndrome as an underlying cause
additionalInvestigations: Dietary and drug history focusing on maize-based diets, alcohol, and isoniazid
Assessment for malabsorption and coexisting B-vitamin deficiencies
Investigation for carcinoid syndrome when suggested clinically
Skin examination and, if uncertain, biopsy to characterise the dermatitis
redFlags: Progressive confusion or dementia indicating advanced central nervous system involvement
Severe diarrhoea with dehydration and electrolyte disturbance
Rapid deterioration in a severely malnourished patient
reference.prognosis: Prompt niacin repletion reverses skin, gastrointestinal, and early neuropsychiatric features quickly; advanced neurological disease may recover incompletely and untreated pellagra can be fatal.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing the rash as a primary photodermatosis and missing the nutritional cause
Overlooking pellagra in patients on isoniazid or with carcinoid syndrome
Failing to treat coexisting deficiencies in the malnourished or alcohol-dependent
Attributing the neuropsychiatric picture solely to dementia or delirium of other cause
